retrieval_flags.k_nearest: HERB_V4_K, 5 unless named. With the step as it stands (persons), with combo, map and both: the number of clusters a list of nearness values is cut into (`v4_walk.levels`). With the older steps: the pick is each query tag's k nearest graph tags, and the dogleg main clusters are switched off in `v4_walk.chain`.
retrieval_flags.offline: HERB_V4_OFFLINE=on reads both query-side answers from the cache and raises where one is missing; off asks the model on a miss.
retrieval_flags.facets: HERB_V4_FACETS, read with the step as it stands: question (the default) lets one reading per facet for the whole question (the middle one of its query tags') decide which facets steer; tag lets each query tag's own reading decide; off uses no facets. The facet net reads the query tags on the laptop; it is no model call.
retrieval_flags.scope_step: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP: call puts the chunks under the products of the second call's places first; off has no scope step and no second call; clouds keeps the chunks under the scopes whose totals are the top group of the clustering and cuts the others, no second call.
retrieval_flags.cloud_shape: HERB_V4_CLOUD_SHAPE, read with scope_step clouds: the shape of each place's numbers before they are added up per scope (as_is, spread, unit, order).
retrieval_flags.cloud_levels: HERB_V4_CLOUD_LEVELS: the levels of the tree gauged, of product, kind, channel; all three unless named.
retrieval_flags.cloud_places: HERB_V4_CLOUD_PLACES: the places gauged (`v4_walk.place_numbers`: tags, description, chunk_desc, question, hits, topic, tags_to_desc); tags and description unless named. HERB_V4_CLOUD_SHAPE may name one shape per place.
retrieval_flags.cloud_groups: HERB_V4_CLOUD_GROUPS: picked lets the clustering pick the number of groups (the largest mean silhouette); two splits the totals in two.
retrieval_flags.hit_stages: HERB_V4_HIT_STAGES, read with scope_step hits: the stages whose hit chunks are gauged over the tree (`_stage_hits`: arm, tags, chunk_desc, question, topic, picked); a stage's hits are the chunks it alone would deliver inside the character budget. The places where the hits gather beyond every random scatter are kept (`v4_walk.scan_clouds`), the others cut, no second call.
retrieval_flags.level_places: HERB_V4_LEVEL_PLACES, read with scope_step levels: the places whose levels are gauged (tags, chunk_desc, question; tags and chunk_desc unless named). The clustering decides what is hit: each list of nearness values is split into levels at its knees (`v4_walk.levels_of`), a level is a 0-1 relevancy, a scope's cloud is its chunks' relevancy added up, the largest clouds are kept with the minorities that share their parent (`v4_walk.level_clouds`), the others cut, no second call. HERB_V4_LEVEL_DEPTH: how many nearest levels count as hit; all unless named.
retrieval_flags.map: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP=map (his 2026-10-11 "/goal reason and research until you find an actual viable solution ... implement that"; his "dont use more ai in the artefact" the same day took it out of use). The border: the chunk descriptions' closeness to the question cut into HERB_V4_K clusters, the branch most of the first cluster sits in, the rest out of the pool (`v4_walk.border_by_nearness`). Then one more model call, the map call: the model reads the border's map (its parts in order, each chunk a label, its description and its tags) and names the chunks an answer would be read from (`query_content.map_request`); labels, no number. The named chunks come first in the model's order; the border's other chunks follow, one from each route in turn (the chunk's closest tag to a query tag, the description, the question). No second (scope) call, no strength, no facet. The description texts are read from a side file, not from the graph.
retrieval_flags.both: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP=both (his 2026-10-10 "now i want to do the both, side by side, together, either cleanly, or overlapping clouds for each step"; overlapping clouds for each step is built): no second call and no strength (`v4_walk.both_sides`). A chunk's nearness through its tags is the closeness of its closest eligible tag to a query tag; by its description, the description's closeness to the query description. Each list is cut into HERB_V4_K clusters and the first is the cloud. Scope step: the scopes both scope clouds hold (the same nearness per scope, the mean of its chunks) that hold a chunk both nearness clouds hold; their branches are the border, the rest is out of the pool; with no such scope nothing is cut. Inside step: both sides cut again over the border; the chunks both clouds hold first, then the chunks one holds, then the rest; inside each the cluster of the chunk's nearness through its tags, then where the query tag's named facet stands among the four facets of that edge, then that nearness.
retrieval_flags.tags: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP=tags (his 2026-10-08 "first tags, then clustering on them, THEN check the scope on all tags ... take the scopes of the greatest cluster(s)? and then after that, we do the facets sorting"): no second call. Per query tag its picked edges in the main cluster of its first facet; per scope the tags of those edges, each once with its closeness, added up; the main cluster of the scopes' values (the dogleg deciding) is kept, the other scopes are out of the pool (`v4_walk.scope_by_tags`); the facets sort inside, as the chain does.
retrieval_flags.cluster: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP=cluster, the step as it stands (his 2026-10-07 "use the structure last, as a vertical cut" / "as a filter", "we can just cluster by scope", "keep minorities if same parents", "i dont think we use the second call if we do this"): no second call. What is hit: the main cluster of the chain's relevance, every chunk's strength in one list, the dogleg deciding (`v4_walk.cluster_hits`; HERB_V4_CLUSTER_PLACES: relevance, tags, chunk_desc, question; relevance unless named). HERB_V4_CLUSTER_READING, his two readings of 2026-10-08 ("indeed, try them"): scopes (the scopes are the clusters; the largest clouds are the main cluster of the clouds' sizes, the dogleg deciding; minorities with the same parent are kept) or formed (the clustering forms the clouds: scopes with hit chunks and the same parent are one cloud). The chunks outside the kept scopes are out of the pool (`v4_walk.scope_clusters`).
retrieval_flags.name: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP=name (his 2026-10-11 "if we take our latest best run, and do that part for scope instead"): no second call. The border is every branch of the tree whose name stands in the question word for word (`scope_by_name`); the chunks outside it are out of the pool, and with no such name nothing is cut. Inside it the order is the chain's (`v4_walk.chain`).
retrieval_flags.combo: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP=combo, the step before the one as it stands (his 2026-10-12 "the combo should fucking work.. So, if we use the chunk-cloud, see if you can find a way to combo or lift with the tags", then "/goal solve this"): no second call, no strength, no facet. Every chunk is handed over as it is. The border is the name step's (`scope_by_name`). Inside it (`v4_walk.cloud_combo`): the chunk descriptions' closeness to the question with the border's names taken out (each replaced by "the" and the tree's word for that level, `_without_names`), and each chunk's closest eligible tag to a query tag, are each cut into HERB_V4_K clusters; a chunk's step is its two levels added; the scope is the parents (a channel, or a product's documents, transcripts, pull requests, links, chats) that hold the majority of the chunks on the first two steps, and inside a step the chunks in scope come first, then the two standings added. The first call's description is embedded and kept in the row and does not enter the order.
retrieval_flags.persons: HERB_V4_SCOPE_STEP=persons, the step as it stands (2026-10-13, under his "/goal solve this"; his 2026-10-11 "what fucking IS missing, is a REAL use of the graph format ... things related to persons etc (or users) and nothing at all is actually using the graph"). The border and the order are the combo step's, with the query's facets on the tags side (2026-10-15/16, his "they are supposed to influence the already existing relationship for chunks and tags" and "how important the facet conecpt is"; `v4_walk.facets_in_equal_closeness`, HERB_V4_FACETS): the facet net reads each query tag against the question and the description; a facet steers when its reading stands in one of that facet's levels over the graph's edges; inside each cluster of the tags side's closeness the chunks are put in order by their edge's places in the steering facets' rankings and the closeness values dealt out in that order. What differs from the combo step besides is what is handed over, in that order (`_hand_over`): no message of a channel apart; of a batch of pull requests only the product's own; of a batch of Slack messages only the conversations that are not about another project's pull request, each conversation whole where it first shows (its messages in the chunk before or after come with it and are not handed over again); any other chunk as it is. From the graph (`product_persons`): a channel is apart when it has employees and none of them is tied to another channel or to a meeting of the product; the product's people are the employees of its other channels and of its meetings. From the records, through the chunk's pointer: a pull request is the product's own when its author is one of the product's people; a conversation is a channel's messages between its long gaps (`v4_walk.conversations`, no length given); it is about another project's when a message of it links to a pull request that is not the product's own and none links to an own pull request or to a document of the product. The agent's find, read off the benchmark's own account of the distraction it holds (arXiv 2506.23139), not his concept; it never reads the question.
